## Introduction

The family planning readiness assessment covered 12 health facilities across Ukerewe and Buchosa District Councils. It examined service availability, commodities, equipment, functionality, documentation, guidelines and provider training. Findings indicate that facilities generally provide several core family planning methods, particularly condoms, implants and oral contraceptives, but readiness is uneven across methods and councils. 

Important gaps exist in permanent methods, IUCD, female condoms, adolescent-friendly services, and specialized family training. The pattern suggests that service provision is constrained not only by demand, but also by weaknesses in commodity security, infrastructure, clinical tools, documentation and workforce competencies.

```{r package}

#Load packages

if(!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, janitor, gtsummary, flextable, inspectdf, scales)

```


```{r data}
#import family planning data

fp_data <- 
  readxl::read_excel(here("data/fp_dataset.xlsx")) |> 
  select(council:q1809_06_asrh, -contains("comment"))

```

## Services availability

Service availability is mixed across the 12 facilities, with differences between councils and contraceptive methods. While condoms, implants and oral combined contraceptives are widely available in most facilities, male sterilization and female condoms are unavailable in Buchosa. Non-hormonal IUCD services are only available in three facilies, two in Buchosa and one Ukerewe whereas emergency pills and cycle beads show stronger availability in Ukerewe. Eleven facilities (91.7%) reported offering adolescent-friendly services.

```{r service availability}

fp_data_clean <-  
  clean_names(fp_data) |> 
  mutate(council = 
           case_when(council == "BUCHOSA" ~ "Buchosa",
                     council == "UKEREWE DC" ~ "Ukerewe",
                     TRUE ~ council)) |> 
  select(-q1802_03_combined_inj) # Tanzania doesn't provide combined contraceptive injections
```

## Supplies and commodities

Commodity availability mirrors service availability, indicating that some service gaps are directly linked to commodity readiness. Male condoms and implants are available in 12 facilities, while oral combined contraceptives and oral progestin-only methods are more available in Ukerewe than Buchosa. Non-hormonal IUCD commodities are present in one facility in each council. Female condoms are absent in Buchosa and available in two Ukerewe facilities. Male sterilization kits are available in one Ukerewe facility and absent in Buchosa. Emergency pills and cycle beads are more available in Ukerewe. These findings suggest inequitable commodity distribution and limitations in method choice, continuity and contraceptive decision-making.

## Equipment 

### Availability

Essential equipment availability presents a significant readiness constraint. Examination beds are relatively well covered, observed in 92% of facilities, while sponge-holding forceps and gallipots/kidney dishes are available in 75%. Tenaculum forceps, speculums, curved scissors, body scales and height boards are available in 67% of facilities. Uterine sounds and blood-pressure machines are available in 58%, while scalpels and examination lamps are present in half of facilities. Thermometers have the lowest availability at 42%. These gaps are important for IUD insertion, client assessment, infection prevention and safe service delivery. Equipment shortages therefore remain a practical barrier to comprehensive family planning readiness.

```{r availability}

# fp_data_clean |>
#   select(availability_of_bp_machine:availability_of_scalpel, 
#          -contains("function")) |> 
#   inspect_cat() |> 
#   show_plot()

# Select and rename the equipment variables cleanly
equip_plot_data <- 
  fp_data_clean |>
  select(
    `Body scale & height board` = q1806_02_scale_height_board_available,
    `BP machine`                = q1806_01_blood_pressure_apparatus_available,
    `Curved scissors`           = q1806_11_curved_scissors_available,
    `Examination bed`           = q1806_04_examination_bed_available,
    `Examination lamp`          = q1806_05_examination_lamp_available,
    `Gallipot / kidney dish`    = q1806_10_gallipot_kidney_dish_available,
    `Scalpel`                   = q1806_12_scalpel_available,
    `Speculum`                  = q1806_06_speculum_available,
    `Sponge holding forceps`    = q1806_09_sponge_holding_forceps_available,
    `Tenaculum forceps`         = q1806_08_tenaculum_forceps_available,
    `Thermometer`               = q1806_03_thermometer_available,
    `Uterine sound`             = q1806_07_uterine_sound_available) |>
  
   
  # Change all 'NA' and "reported_not seen" to "not_available"
  
mutate(
  across(
    everything(),
    ~ case_when(
        is.na(.) ~ "not_available",
        . == "reported_not_seen" ~ "not_available",
        TRUE ~ as.character(.)
      )
  )
) |> 
  
  
  # Pivot to long format
pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "equipment",
    values_to = "status") |>
  filter(!is.na(status)) |>
  
  mutate(
  status = case_when(
    status == "observed" ~ "Observed",
    status == "not_available" ~ "Not available",
    TRUE ~ status)) |> 
  
  # Calculate counts and percentages per equipment
  count(equipment, status) |>
  group_by(equipment) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,
    
    # Make "Not available" negative so it diverges to the left
    diverging_pct = if_else(status == "Observed", pct, -pct),
    
    # Create clean percentage labels
    label_text = paste0(round(pct, 0), "%"),
    
    # Helper column to sort bars from highest to lowest "Observed" %
    observed_pct = sum(pct[status == "Observed"])) |> 
  
  ungroup()

# 4. Plot the diverging bar chart

equipment_plot <- 
  ggplot(equip_plot_data, 
         aes(x = reorder(equipment, observed_pct),
             y = diverging_pct,
             fill = factor(status, levels = c("Not available", "Observed")))) +
  
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  
  # Add vertical center line at 0%
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.6) +
  
  # Add percentage labels inside/next to bars
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = label_text,
      hjust = if_else(status == "Observed", -0.2, 1.2)
    ),
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray20"
  ) +
  
  # Format x-axis (flipped) to show positive percentages on both sides
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-105, 115),
    breaks = seq(-100, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(abs(x), "%")
  ) +
  
  # Use a clean, accessible two-color palette
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Not available" = "#E07A5F", "Observed" = "#2A9D8F"),
    name = "Availability Status"
  ) +
  
  coord_flip() +
  
  labs(
    title = "Figure 4. Availability of Essential Medical Equipment",
    subtitle = "% of facilities where equipment was observed versus not available",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percentage of Facilities"
  ) +
  
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90", linetype = "dashed")
  )

# Display the chart
equipment_plot

# Save the figure in the output folder
ggsave(
  filename = "equipment.jpg",
  plot = equipment_plot,
  path = "output",
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)


```

### Functionality

Functionality among available equipment was strong, suggesting that the main challenge is procurement or distribution rather than widespread equipment failure. Uterine sounds, thermometers, tenaculum forceps, sponge-holding forceps, speculums, gallipots/kidney dishes, examination beds, curved scissors and blood-pressure machines were 100% functional among assessed items. However, body scales and height boards were 88% functional, while examination lamps were only 67% functional. The distinction between availability and functionality is important: even when equipment works, it cannot support services if it is absent. Priority should therefore be given to closing availability gaps while maintaining maintenance systems. This highlights need for planned equipment maintenance.

```{r functionality}


functionality_data <- 
fp_data_clean |>
  select(q1806_01_blood_pressure_apparatus_available:q1806_12_scalpel_functional, 
         -contains("_available")) |> 
  rename (
    `Body scale & height board` = q1806_02_scale_height_board_functional,
    `BP machine`                = q1806_01_blood_pressure_apparatus_functional,
    `Curved scissors`           = q1806_11_curved_scissors_functional,
    `Examination bed`           = q1806_04_examination_bed_functional,
    `Examination lamp`          = q1806_05_examination_lamp_functional,
    `Gallipot / kidney dish`    = q1806_10_gallipot_kidney_dish_functional,
    `Scalpel`                   = q1806_12_scalpel_functional,
    `Speculum`                  = q1806_06_speculum_functional,
    `Sponge holding forceps`    = q1806_09_sponge_holding_forceps_functional,
    `Tenaculum forceps`         = q1806_08_tenaculum_forceps_functional,,
    `Thermometer`               = q1806_03_thermometer_functional,
    `Uterine sound`             = q1806_07_uterine_sound_functional) |> 
  
  
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "item",
    values_to = "status") |> 
  filter(!is.na(status))


# Clean labels, calculate percentages, and sort by functional rate
plot_data <- 
  functionality_data |>
  mutate(
    
    # Change "Yes" -> "Functional" and "No" -> "Non-functional"
    status = factor(
      status,
      levels = c("yes", "no"),
      labels = c("Functional", "Non-functional")
    )
  ) |>
  count(item, status) |>
  group_by(item) |>
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    pct = n / total,
    
    # Add sample size (n) to the label since NAs were dropped
    item_label = paste0(item, " (n=", total, ")"),
    
    # Capture the percentage of "Functional" to sort bars cleanly
    sort_val = pct[status == "Functional"][1]
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(sort_val = ifelse(is.na(sort_val), 0, sort_val))

# Create the horizontal stacked bar chart
functionality_plot <- 
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = pct, 
                      y = reorder(item_label, sort_val), fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = ifelse(pct >= 0.06, percent(pct, accuracy = 1), "")),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.3
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 5. Operational Status of Available Medical Equipment",
    subtitle = "Proportion of functional versus non-functional items",
    x = "Percentage out of assessed Equipment",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

# Display the chart
functionality_plot


# Save the figure in the output folder
ggsave(
  filename = "functionality.jpg",
  plot = functionality_plot,
  path = "output",
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)


```

## Guidelines and Medical Records

Documentation and guideline readiness is uneven. Client records/files are available in 92% of facilities and checklists/job aids in 67%, indicating stronger foundation for recording and supporting service delivery. However, the national family planning guideline is observed in 42% of facilities, while other family planning guidelines are available in 25%. Adolescent reproductive health guidance is particularly weak: both national and adolescent reproductive guidelines are observed in only 8% of facilities. This creates a risk that providers may deliver services without consistent access to standards, for adolescents and care. Guideline availability and use should therefore be strengthened alongside documentation quality.


```{r}

# 1. Select HMIS and guideline columns
hmis_data <- 
  fp_data_clean |> 
  select(
    q1808_01_national_fp_guidelines_available:
      q1808_06_client_records_available
  )


# 2. Rename and clean variables
hmis_plot_data <- 
  hmis_data |>
  select(
    `Checklist/Job aids` = q1808_03_fp_checklist_job_aids_available,
    `National family planning\n guideline` = 
      q1808_01_national_fp_guidelines_available,
    `Other family planning\n guideline` = 
      q1808_02_other_fp_guidelines_available,
    `National adolescent\n reproductive guideline` = 
      q1808_04_national_adolescent_guidelines_available,
    `Other adolescent\n reproductive guidelines` =
      q1808_05_other_adolescent_guidelines_available,
    `Clients' records/files` = q1808_06_client_records_available
  ) |>

  # Replace NA and reported_not_seen
  mutate(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ case_when(
        is.na(.) ~ "not_available",
        as.character(.) == "reported_not_seen" ~ "not_available",
        TRUE ~ as.character(.)
      )
    )
  ) |>

  # 3. Reshape to long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "hmis",
    values_to = "status"
  ) |>

  # 4. Standardise response categories
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      status == "observed" ~ "Observed",
      status == "not_available" ~ "Not available",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(status)) |>

  # 5. Calculate counts and percentages
  count(hmis, status) |>
  group_by(hmis) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n / sum(n) * 100,

    diverging_pct = if_else(
      status == "Observed",
      pct,
      -pct
    ),

    label_text = paste0(round(pct), "%"),

    observed_pct = sum(
      pct[status == "Observed"],
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()


# 6. Plot diverging bar chart
hmis_plot <- 
  ggplot(
    hmis_plot_data,
    aes(
      x = reorder(hmis, observed_pct),
      y = diverging_pct,
      fill = factor(
        status,
        levels = c("Not available", "Observed")
      )
    )
  ) +

  geom_col(width = 0.7) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    color = "gray30",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = label_text,
      hjust = if_else(
        status == "Observed",
        -0.2,
        1.2
      )
    ),
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray20"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-105, 115),
    breaks = seq(-100, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(abs(x), "%")
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Not available" = "#E07A5F",
      "Observed" = "#2A9D8F"
    ),
    name = "Availability Status"
  ) +

  coord_flip(clip = "off") +

  labs(
    title = "Figure 6. Availability of HMIS Tools and Clinical Guidelines",
    subtitle = "% of facilities with observed vs. unavailable tools and guidelines",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percentage of Facilities"
  ) +

  theme_classic() +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40", size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linetype = "dashed"
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)
  )


# 7. Display chart
hmis_plot


# 8. Save figure
ggsave(
  filename = "hmis.jpg",
  plot = hmis_plot,
  path = "output",
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

```


## Family Planning Training

Training gaps emerged as a major weakness in facility readiness to provide family planning services. In Buchosa, all six facilities (100%) reported no training in hormonal and non-hormonal IUDs, implants, and adolescent-friendly services in the past two years. For permanent family planning methods, including male and female sterilization, five of the six facilities (83%) lacked recent training, with only one facility reporting to have received capacity building in these areas. The situation was more pronounced in Ukerewe, where all six facilities (100%) lacked recent training across all six assessed areas, including IUDs, implants, adolescent-friendly services, and male and female sterilization. 

These findings indicate that service and commodity availability may not translate into provision where specialized skills are required. The training pattern also limits method choice, particularly for adolescents and clients seeking permanent or IUD methods. A competency-based, training and mentorship plan is therefore essential.


```{r trainings}

# Select relevant columns
training_data <- 
  fp_data_clean |> 
  select(
    council, 
    q1809_01_iucd_hormonal:q1809_06_asrh)

# Rename, pivot, calculate percentages before filtering, and plot
training_gaps_plot <- 
  training_data |>
  rename(
    `IUCD hormonal training` = q1809_01_iucd_hormonal,
    
    `IUCD non-hormonal training` = q1809_02_iucd_nonhormonal,
    
    `Male sterilization training` = q1809_03_male_sterilization,
    
    `Female sterilization training` = q1809_04_female_sterilization,
    
    `Adolescent friendly services training` = q1809_06_asrh,
    
    `Implant training` = q1809_05_implants
  ) |> 
  
  # Reshape to long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -council,
    names_to = "training",
    values_to = "status"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(status)) |>
  
  # Calculate counts and percentages BEFORE filtering to "No"
  count(council, training, status) |>
  group_by(council, training) |>
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    pct = n / total,
    # Create clean label showing both percentage and fraction: e.g., "83% (5/6)"
    bar_label = paste0(round(pct * 100, 0), "% (", n, "/", total, ")")
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  
  # Now keep only facilities that lacked training ("No")
  filter(status == "no") |> 
  
  # Plot the grouped percentage bar chart
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = reorder(training, pct), y = pct, fill = council)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.78), width = 0.7) +
  
  # Add direct percentage and count labels next to each bar
  geom_text(
    aes(label = bar_label),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.78),
    hjust = -0.1,
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray20"
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(),
    limits = c(0, 1.22), # Extra room on right for text labels
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Buchosa" = "#E07A5F", "Ukerewe" = "#2A9D8F")
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Figure 7. Family Planning Training Gaps by District Council",
    subtitle = "% of facilities lacking training in the past 2 years",
    x = NULL, 
    y = "Percentage of Facilities",
    fill = "District Council"
  ) +
  
  coord_flip() +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray40"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "gray90", linetype = "dashed")
  )

# Display the chart
training_gaps_plot 


# Save the figure in the output folder
ggsave(
  filename = "training_gaps.jpg",
  plot = training_gaps_plot,
  path = "output",
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)


```

## Discussion

Overall, the assessment demonstrates that family planning readiness is multidimensional and cannot be judged by service availability alone. Facilities may have commodities or functioning equipment while lacking the full package required for safe, informed and equitable care. Ukerewe generally shows broader availability for several services and commodities, whereas Buchosa has gaps. Across both councils, IUD services, permanent methods, adolescent-friendly care, guidelines and provider training require attention. The contrast between high functionality of available equipment and low equipment availability suggests supply and distribution weaknesses. Strengthening readiness should therefore combine commodity and equipment systems with clinical capacity, standards, documentation and supportive supervision.


## Recommendations

The health system should prioritize a readiness improvement plan with clear responsibilities, timelines and monitoring indicators across the following strategic areas:

* Quantification and redistribution/procurement of family planning commodities and equipment, prioritizing IUCDs supplies, sterilization kits, examination lamps, thermometers, uterine sounds and blood-pressure machines. 

* Competency-based training and mentorship for IUCDs insertion, implants, permanent methods and adolescent-friendly services. 

* Ensure every facility has current national family planning and adolescent reproductive health guidelines, checklists and job aids. 

* Strengthen stock monitoring, equipment maintenance and supportive supervision. 

* Review progress quarterly using readiness indicators and address gaps at facility level through R/CHMT supervisions.


## Conclusion

The assessment shows that family planning readiness across the 12 facilities is partial. Core methods such as implants, male condoms and oral contraceptives are established, but access to IUCDs, permanent methods and female condoms remains limited. Commodity gaps correspond with service gaps, while equipment availability is weaker than equipment functionality. Documentation is stronger than access to clinical and adolescent guidelines, and training gaps are widespread. These findings point to health system constraints that require coordinated action rather than isolated interventions. Improving commodity security, equipment availability, provider competence, guideline access and supportive supervision will be critical to achieving equitable and quality family planning services
